- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-history, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% to later forecast days.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ from prior day) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak for next 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.5 → 0.0 → 0.5), model often misjudges direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend shift, not absolute value.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early drop (first 5 days) after spike, model often overcorrects; reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 1–4% to match observed decay.
